lines.text: Here's how to use Opus five point five as your daily driver, in under sixty seconds.
Say growth slowed at your retail company, and your manager has four theories to test.
Habit one: put everything in your first message. Say what the goal is, what the finished output looks like, and when to stop and ask.
Habit two: drop "think hard." Thinking is always on, and removing the phrase made replies start sooner, with no clear drop in quality.
Habit three: leave effort on Medium, the default. In testing, Medium matched or beat Opus five at High, so move up only when Medium stalls.
Habit four: ask for the finished file, not an outline.
Claude tested all four theories against your sales data, and none held up, though one couldn't be fully ruled out.
It also found what nobody had raised. New stores opened too close to old ones and pulled sales away.
